title: Colour
scope: Colour roles and their values; contrast in the AA and AAA themes; the light and dark colour schemes; the colour of surfaces, text, links, states, focus, selection, status, gradients, shadows, code and charts; forced colours mode; and the tokens that carry a colour.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Sensory Characteristics
sources.uses: Instructions do not rely solely on shape, colour, size, visual location, orientation or sound

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Use of Color
sources.uses: Colour is not the only visual means of conveying information; hue alone needs a second cue; lightness at 3:1 counts as a second cue

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Contrast (Minimum)
sources.uses: Text contrast in the AA theme, the definition of the contrast ratio, unrounded thresholds, large-scale text, logotypes and inactive components

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Contrast (Enhanced)
sources.uses: Text contrast in the AAA theme

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Non-text Contrast
sources.uses: Contrast of what identifies a component and its states, and of the parts of a graphic required to understand it; a gradient is tested at its least contrasting area

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Pause, Stop, Hide
sources.uses: Moving content that starts automatically, lasts more than five seconds and is presented in parallel with other content can be paused, stopped or hidden

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Three Flashes or Below Threshold
sources.uses: No more than three flashes in any second; the definition of a saturated red

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Focus Appearance
sources.uses: Size of the focus indicator and its 3:1 contrast between the focused and unfocused states

sources.title: WCAG Technique C40: Creating a two-color focus indicator to ensure sufficient contrast with all components
sources.uses: Two indicator colours at least 9:1 apart, so one meets 3:1 against any solid background; not to rely on box-shadow alone, which forced colour modes suppress
sources.note: Sufficient for 1.4.11, 2.4.7 and 2.4.13. Its guarantee holds only over one solid background colour; over an image or a gradient the indicator is compared pixel by pixel.

sources.title: WCAG Technique G183: Using a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 to distinguish inline text links from surrounding text
sources.uses: An inline link marked by colour alone needs 3:1 against the text around it; otherwise another cue, such as an underline

sources.title: WCAG 3.0
sources.uses: Its contrast method is still to be determined, so the WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio stays the measure

sources.title: CSS Color Module Level 4
sources.uses: The system colours that name colour roles, the Oklab and OKLCH colour spaces, colour interpolation (legacy sRGB syntax mixes in sRGB) and gamut mapping

sources.title: CSS Color Adjustment Module Level 1
sources.uses: `color-scheme`, forced colours mode and `forced-color-adjust`; in forced colours mode `box-shadow` and `text-shadow` compute to `none`, and `background-image` too unless it contains a `url()`

sources.title: Media Queries Level 5
sources.uses: `prefers-contrast` (an unqualified query also matches `less`), `prefers-color-scheme` and `forced-colors`

sources.title: Design Tokens Format Module
sources.uses: The `color` type (colour space, components, alpha, hex fallback) and the `gradient`, `shadow` and `border` types that hold a colour
sources.note: designtokens.org didn't load, so it was read from the spec's source on GitHub (the editor's draft, not the 2025.10 snapshot). Naming, gamut mapping, interpolation and the resolver were read through a summarising fetch only.

sources.title: Geolocation
sources.uses: A location is shared only with the express permission of the user, only in a secure context, and with an embedded frame only where the host page allows it
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: Privacy Principles
sources.uses: Data minimisation: only the data needed for the user's goal is taken
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: CSS Positioned Layout Module Level 4
sources.uses: The top layer and the `::backdrop` pseudo-element
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: Selectors Level 4
sources.uses: The `:hover` and `:active` pseudo-classes
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch: the opening sentences of sections 9.1 and 9.2 only.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Headings and Labels
sources.uses: A label describes its topic or purpose
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Name, Role, Value
sources.uses: A state the user can set can be set programmatically, and a change of it is notified to user agents and assistive technologies
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: WCAG technique F83: Failure of Success Criterion 1.4.3 and 1.4.6 due to using background images that do not provide sufficient contrast with foreground text (or images of text)
sources.uses: Text over a background image is tested where the image is most like the text: its darkest area for dark text, its lightest for light text
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Visual Presentation (Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.8)
sources.uses: The user can select foreground and background colours, by a mechanism the browser or another user agent may provide
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch. The page names no operating system mode and no forced colours mode.

sources.title: CSS Images Module Level 4
sources.uses: A gradient states its colour interpolation method, such as `in oklab` or `in oklch`
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch, sections 3.1 to 3.2.1 only. The hue direction of a polar colour space was not seen there.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2, Animation from Interactions
sources.uses: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled; a change of colour, blurring or opacity that does not change the perceived size, shape or position of an element is not motion animation

sources.title: CSS Basic User Interface Module Level 4
sources.uses: `accent-color`, for the widgets a platform draws with an accent colour, and `caret-color`, whose `auto` value uses `currentColor`
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch. The section read does not list the form controls `accent-color` applies to.

sources.title: CSS Scrollbars Styling Module Level 1
sources.uses: `scrollbar-color`: with `auto` the user agent determines the colours of the scrollbar
sources.note: Read through a summarising fetch; its quotes were not re-checked against the page.

sources.title: Brettel, Vienot and Mollon, Computerized simulation of color appearance for dichromats, Journal of the Optical Society of America A 14(10), 1997
sources.uses: A method to simulate how red-blind, green-blind and blue-blind people see a colour
sources.note: Only the abstract was read. Per the abstract, a red-blind and a green-blind observer tested the simulation; the blue-blind case was not tested on an observer.

sources.title: Vienot, Brettel and Mollon, Digital video colourmaps for checking the legibility of displays by dichromats, Color Research and Application 24(4), 1999
sources.uses: A method to simulate on a display how red-blind and green-blind people see a colour
sources.note: The publisher's page did not load; title, authors and journal were seen in metadata records only, and the content was not read.

sources.title: Council Directive 92/58/EEC of 24 June 1992 on the minimum requirements for the provision of safety and/or health signs at work
sources.uses: Red for prohibition and danger, yellow or amber for warning, green for no danger, blue for mandatory signs
sources.note: The meanings were read on 2026-11-16 (DEC-187). On 2026-11-24 a second reader got no text from EUR-Lex and saw only the title, the date and the annex titles on the EU-OSHA summary page.

sources.title: Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 2009 edition, Section 1A.12 Color Code (US Federal Highway Administration)
sources.uses: Red for stop or prohibition, yellow for warning, green for permitted movement and direction guidance, blue for road user services guidance
sources.note: Blue also covers tourist information and evacuation routes there.

sources.title: 23 CFR Part 655, Subpart F, Appendix: Alternate Method of Determining the Color of Retroreflective Sign Materials and Pavement Marking Materials
sources.uses: CIE chromaticity regions of traffic sign colours, the source of the status hues with 49 CFR 172
sources.note: Read on the copy of the Legal Information Institute; ecfr.gov did not load.

sources.title: 49 CFR Part 172, Appendix A: Office of Hazardous Materials Transportation Color Tolerance Charts and Tables
sources.uses: Munsell notations and CIE coordinates of hazard label colours, the source of the status hues with 23 CFR 655
sources.note: Read on the copy of the Legal Information Institute; ecfr.gov did not load.

sources.title: Kingdom, Beauce and Hunter, Colour vision brings clarity to shadows, Perception 33(8), 2004
sources.uses: Colour changes typically occur at the edges of objects and not of shadows, so a change of luminance with no change of colour tends to be read as lighting
sources.note: Only the abstract was read. It states a regularity the visual system uses, not an absolute rule.

sources.title: Bae, Olkkonen, Allred and Flombaum, Why some colors appear more memorable than others: a model combining categories and particulars in color working memory, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 144(4), 2015
sources.uses: A remembered colour is biased toward the centre of its colour category
sources.note: Only the abstract was read. The same bias appears without a memory delay; memory makes it larger.

sources.title: Uchikawa, Purity discrimination: successive vs simultaneous comparison method, Vision Research 23(1), 1983
sources.uses: Colours seen one after the other need a difference about 1.5 to 2 times larger to be told apart than colours seen side by side
sources.note: Only the abstract was read.

sources.title: Berlin and Kay, Basic Color Terms: Their Universality and Evolution, University of California Press, 1969
sources.uses: The idea of a small set of basic colour terms
sources.note: A book, not read: only a catalogue summary was seen.

sources.title: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Solar Calculator, calculation details
sources.uses: Sunrise and sunset are computed from a date and a place, to within a minute between 72 degrees north and south
sources.note: The page says the calculator is no longer actively maintained and that observed values may differ from the computed ones.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation), Article 4(1)
sources.uses: Location data is named among the identifiers that make data personal
sources.note: Read on 2026-11-22 (DEC-182). On 2026-11-24 a second reader got no text from EUR-Lex.

sources.title: HashiCorp, HCP Brand Guidelines: Brand Logos
sources.uses: A horizontal full logo as the primary, a vertical one when space requires, the mark alone where the audience knows the brand, and no other colours or tints
sources.note: Concepts only.

sources.title: National Wildlife Federation Brand Guide: Primary Logo and Logomark
sources.uses: Horizontal and vertical configurations, colour and reversed versions, and choosing the version that is clearest against its background
sources.note: Concepts only.

sources.title: Ramachandran, Perception of shape from shading, Nature 331, 1988
sources.uses: The visual system assumes one light source for the whole image
sources.note: Only the abstract was read; it does not say the light comes from above.

sources.title: Morgenstern, Murray and Harris, The human visual system's assumption that light comes from above is weak, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 108(30), 2011
sources.uses: The assumption of a light from above is weak, and barely visible lighting cues override it
sources.note: Only the abstract was read.
